title: 4D Live Fluorescence Microscopy for Imaging Yeast Cellular Responses
author: Alvarado-Cartagena, Huppenbauer, et al.
materials: Timing: 30 min after addition of rapamycin

steps.title: Prepare YPD liquid media
steps.instruction: Mix 10 g yeast extract, 20 g bacter peptone, and distilled water in a beaker up to 950 mL. Transfer to a 500 mL bottle, autoclave, let cool to room temperature, then add 50 mL sterile 40 % glucose solution before use.

steps.title: Prepare YPD agar plates
steps.instruction: In a 2000 mL flask combine 10 g yeast extract, 20 g bacter peptone, 20 g bacter agar, and distilled water up to 950 mL. Autoclave, then add 50 mL sterile 40 % glucose and stir with a magnetic bar until the mixture cools. Pour into sterile Petri dishes avoiding air bubbles, let plates dry at room temperature for 1–2 days, then store at 4 °C. Ensure the glucose solution is sterile before addition.

steps.title: Streak strain on YPD plates
steps.instruction: Streak the desired yeast strain from glycerol stock onto prepared YPD plates and incubate 2–3 days at 30 °C. Keep plates in sealed plastic bags during and after incubation to prevent drying.

steps.title: Inoculate overnight culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single colony and inoculate into 3 mL YPD liquid medium in a test tube. Incubate with rotation at 30 °C for 6–16 hours.

steps.title: Dilute and grow to mid‑log
steps.instruction: Measure the OD₆₀₀ of the overnight culture. Dilute to an OD₆₀₀ of 0.002 using 25–30 mL fresh YPD in a 50 mL flask. Incubate at 28 °C with shaking at 200 rpm for 16–18 hours until the culture reaches OD₆₀₀ 0.5–0.8. (Do not use a saturated culture.)

steps.title: Induce stress and stain lysosomes
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.5–1 mL of the mid‑log culture to a clean tube. Add rapamycin to a final concentration of 200 nM and incubate at 28 °C with shaking for 30 minutes. For lysosomal membrane staining, add FM4‑64 simultaneously with rapamycin; for lumen staining, add CMAC 15–30 minutes before the end of the rapamycin incubation.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the stained culture at 800 rpm for 2 minutes in a 1 mL microtube. For FM4‑64‑stained cells, discard the supernatant and wash once with 1 mL YPD + rapamycin; for CMAC‑stained cells, no wash is required.

steps.title: Mount cells on microscopy slide
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in YPD + rapamycin by gentle pipetting. Pipette 1.6 µL of the suspension onto a clean glass slide, cover with an 18 × 18 mm cover glass, and avoid air bubbles. No sonication is needed.

steps.title: Set up microscope for imaging
steps.instruction: Place a drop of immersion oil on the cover glass, mount the slide on a spinning‑disk confocal microscope, and focus using a 65× oil objective. Expect to see ~20 cells per field; typical cell diameter 5–10 µm, vacuole 2–3 µm, engulfed cargo ~0.82 µm. Acquire videos starting 30 minutes after rapamycin addition. Include untreated control cells prepared identically but without rapamycin.

description: The following protocol describes the steps of cell preparation, video capture, and analysis of micro-autophagic events in live budding yeast S. cerevisiae using 3D time-lapse, using a spinning disk fluorescence confocal microscope.1
